claims.why_not_priced: The pre-print drift is the whole of the evidence the market has been acting on, and this name has no captured sell-side preview, no news document and no consensus figure other than an automated estimize relay of $1.14 whose stated report date, 08/27, is wrong. Against that, a peer beat landed a week earlier and the company itself has disclosed nothing negative. The reason I sign it positive rather than zero is the shape of the historical distribution: in seven prints the downside has never exceeded -3.98% while the upside has twice exceeded 8%, so the pre-print markdown has repeatedly not been validated by the print. I am keeping the number to half the median because this is genuinely weak: the finding rests on one retail message for the peer read-through, and the drawdown itself - a JP Morgan downgrade, Walmart cutting prices into the discount channel, 'the next Big Lots' - is a real bear case that the print will not settle.
claims.independence: From a different source in the same corpus: a 2026-08-24 message reports Fidelity increasing its OLLI holding by 29% in the prior quarter, and the filings index independently shows two SCHEDULE 13G/A filings inside one week (2026-08-06 and 2026-08-13), both consistent with institutions adding into the drawdown rather than leaving.
